answer: The bug was in `matches_req` where it returned `true` instead of `false` when a version failed to match one of the requirement's comparators. I corrected the logic to return `false` immediately upon a mismatch.

The bug was in `semver::eval::matches_req`, where it returned `true` instead of `false` when a comparator did not match the version. I corrected this to return `false` immediately upon finding a non-matching comparator.

The bug was in the `matches_req` function in `src/eval.rs`. The loop that checked if a version matched all comparators in a requirement was returning `true` as soon as it found a comparator that did *not* match, instead of returning `false`. I corrected this to return `false` when any comparator fails to match the version.
